blocks.text: When the machine had two shores and a road there and back, the peoples, little by little, began to ask for the circle. Not all of them. Not all at once. The way you ask for a fruit: one, then another, with a harm or a longing named.

blocks.text: First came two of those who waited for water: the woman with the broad forehead, who still lived beside the dry hollow, and one of those who had gone off to look for a real sea and hadn't found it. They arrived at El Estacio, asked for air, and Lía took them to the Mar Menor at sunset, when the water was copper-coloured. The woman with the broad forehead didn't kneel. She sat on the shore, wet her hands, and was silent for a long while, which is one way of drinking.

They arrived at El Estacio, asked for air, and Lía took them to the Mar Menor at sunset, when the water was copper-coloured. The woman with the broad forehead didn't kneel. blocks.text: “Our hollow was a portrait of this,” she said at last. “This doesn't fit in a hollow. Even so, I'm going back to mine. There, the waiting is ours. Here, the water belongs to everyone, and to no one, and I'm not going to stay and possess it. I only wanted to know that it really existed.”

blocks.text: The one who had walked in search of a sea cried, without shame, and asked permission to fish for a day in Andrés's boat. They gave it to him. The engine, the plate, the rope. When he came back, he said he was no longer looking for a water: he had set foot in one, and that was enough for him to go on, on his red ground, opening paths that might lead to no plate at all, and were paths all the same.

blocks.text: Then came three of those who fished on the rafts. They brought a net, not an altar bowl, and asked to cast it here one afternoon, and you could see their trade, and you could also see the impulse to leave an offering in the boat, which Andrés headed off with a gentle gesture, the gesture of someone teaching a knot again. They left with real salt on their skin, and no new owner.

blocks.text: “So the founder's tale was true. The sun goes. I'm glad I came to watch it leave, and to know that tomorrow it comes back, not as a law but as a fact.”

blocks.text: From the almost-identical house nobody came at first. They sent a message: they were afraid this shore, dirty and slow, would undo their polished village. Lía answered, through the technician, that nobody was forcing them, and that if they came they would see the wrong clock and the water with its seaweed, and nobody was going to remove them so that they would feel at home. After a while a woman came with a cup without a crack, saw the cracked one, and asked, with a polite strangeness, to be taught not to improve so much. They left the cup from here in her hands for a while, and she gave it back, and returned to her valley, perhaps a little less picture-postcard, perhaps not. That was no longer this kitchen's business.

blocks.text: From the people of the chip came the one who had said “cold” and had learned his name again. He arrived with no Earth archive, or very little, and the Mar Menor didn't bring him an old memory: it brought him a present. He said “salt”, as he had said “cold”, and laughed, and didn't want anyone putting an office memory in his chest. He left light, with one more word.

blocks.text: From the hillside of faces, no Andrés was allowed to come. A young Vicente was allowed to come, the one who had learned not to answer to a name that wasn't his, and an Eva who wasn't Eva. Andrés, the one of the shore, received them with coffee and without keys, as Lía had said. The young man looked at Vicente's door, the real one, shut, and didn't ask to go in. He said his name, clearly, and that was enough for the courtyard not to turn into a mirror.

blocks.text: The people of the priceless garden first sent a question, not a body: “May we?” Lía answered yes, if they asked, and if they accepted a no to an extra basket. Two came, brought seeds, asked where to leave them, and left them where they were told, not on every table.

blocks.text: Meanwhile Nexum wanted a register of arrivals, a stamp, a “reintegration of origin”. Lía planted herself in the warehouse, with the same words as on the Moon, turned toward a circle:
blocks.html: Meanwhile Nexum wanted a register of arrivals, a stamp, a “reintegration of origin”. Lía planted herself in the warehouse, with the same words as on the Moon, turned toward a circle:

blocks.text: “They aren't a product of Nexum origin. They're people who ask. If there's to be a stamp, let it be a coffee, and a ‘may I?’, and a no when it's needed. Nothing more.”
blocks.html: “They aren't a product of Nexum origin. They're people who ask. If there's to be a stamp, let it be a coffee, and a ‘may I?’, and a no when it's needed. Nothing more.”

blocks.text: Helena, from her stairs, confirmed in a note that she wouldn't sign the stamp. The stamp, for now, wasn't imposed. The circle, for now, remained a road, not a shop counter.

blocks.text: *If the peoples come to check a memory and go back to their hollow, their raft, their strip, what have they found: a home, or proof that their own shore is enough too? And if only one stays, or none, is that fidelity to what was sown, or a timidity that doesn't dare to live here?*

blocks.text: *People from several peoples have crossed. They have drunk, fished, watched the sun set, said “salt”, said a name that wasn't Andrés. The woman from the almost-identical house has touched a cracked cup. Nexum wanted a stamp, and for now it has not been imposed. That is the fact.*

blocks.text: After those weeks, Andrés sat on the doorstep with Aya and saw the promenade a little fuller, not with an army but with visitors who left again. The shore had not turned into an imperial port. It had turned, at times, into a broad afternoon tea. He, who had stayed to be the man of here, understood that staying was this too: opening, not completely, and not holding on. The Mar Menor, at that hour, was black and still, and once again looked like a road, now running in two directions, and even so belonging to no one.
